releases.headline: Set up with one sign-in, avoid building the same work twice, and use the Void collection for free
highlights: Start here can install Codex, Claude Code, Grok or Antigravity, sign you in and check the connection. "Use for the whole studio" then sends chat, mapping, planning, agents and coding through that one subscription.

Build it in Vibe decides whether a request is one task or two to six steps, and a Plan in flight card follows the steps. New app makes a project folder, starts Git and sends your description as the first build.
When you reopen a project, Studio reports the commits, edits and coding sessions made while it was closed. It checks queued cards against that work so finished work is not rebuilt.

There are four permission modes: Always ask, Accept per task, Auto and Elevated only. Automatic decisions come with a Why and an Undo. Mefi learns from your answers, and the desk can settle routine agent questions.
Every theme and node style is free, including the Void collection. Trace shows Studio's logs in one viewer, and Friends › Your PCs with Sync this PC keeps your PCs in step with GitHub.

releases.headline: A media queue, live tree controls and tools for each agent
highlights: An Up next queue for copied links and YouTube results. It has Play, Queue next and a built-in YouTube explorer, and it moves on to the next item by itself.
The node tree can move with the music or a video, in ring, wave or spiral shapes, with controls for size, spacing and position.
Separate transparency and brightness sliders for the tree, the wires and the video, plus optional node outlines.
You can drop text and code files into Home, Vibe and Plans. Planning reads fresh project excerpts and any files you name.
Each agent role can have its own web search, project read permission and allowed MCP tools.

releases.headline: Vibe mode and remastered node styles
highlights: Vibe mode is one calm workspace for conversation, new tasks, live work and decisions, and the full Build workspace is one switch away.
You answer agents' decisions in a drawer inside Vibe. It shows the question, the task it blocks and the recommended option first.
Vibe shows what is stopping the agents and offers the fix in place: Start agents, Resume or Connect an AI.
All eight node styles were remastered with their own shapes, motion, wires and finish effects, including light-theme contrast and reduced motion.
Plans can be archived and restored. There is also a 40-second product showreel.

releases.headline: The Agent Brain: watch your agents work and keep what worked
highlights: The Agent brain view (key J) shows a task's pipeline from the top down. Sub-agents go out, report back up the tree, and a desk worker helps the ones that get stuck.
The Playbook files every verified pipeline as a recipe, so the next task of the same kind starts from what worked.
A project map is built from your git history and your agents' work. Home shows it beside the conversation, with Work on this region.
A companion lives in the menu. It greets you with what happened while you were away and keeps one Needs you list with the actions right there.
The Links player plays YouTube, Spotify, SoundCloud and Vimeo. Home became glass over the live node tree, and the tree can move to your music.

releases.headline: The Discord community link, a regrouped menu and a safer app
highlights: Settings › Community links your Discord account to the Void Engine server through Discord's own login, and nothing reaches Discord until you link. Members got the Void collection, which later became free for everyone in 0.4.4.
The menu was regrouped into Home, Work, Live, Models and Settings, with Search Studio on Ctrl K.
Owner controls for the loop guard. Duplicate cards and repeating work now reach you as one question instead of looping.
Each task shows its run history: who ran it, how it ended and what it changed.
A Usage popover for every provider. Child processes no longer see Studio's keys, and the web preview is local-only.

releases.headline: One navigation rail, Brain maps as a real node editor, and ad-free radio
highlights: One rail down the left edge replaces three separate menus.
Brain maps became a node editor you can pan and zoom, for editing how the agent pipeline decides things.
Ad-free radio from SomaFM and Radio Paradise. If a stream drops, a backup mirror crossfades in.
Planning and reading can each use their own AI provider, and OpenCode Zen became a route.
A loop guard stops cards that keep failing and explains how to release them.

releases.headline: First public release: a portable Windows build with an in-app updater
highlights: A portable Windows download. The in-app updater checks each release's SHA-256 before installing it.
Brain maps: the agent pipeline as an editable graph, and Build with AI can draft one from a sentence.
A seven-stop Start here walkthrough with a Walk with me coach.
Command view's live node tree. Finished work waits in a verification stage, with evidence, before it counts as done.
Routing across many providers (z.ai, OpenCode Go, the Claude Code, Codex, Grok and Antigravity CLIs, LM Studio, custom endpoints), plus a usage tracker.
